findings.finding: The durable branch locks before read, imports latest disk into a temporary base registry, applies one operation, writes only changed requests, and assigns self.inner only after success. Errors preserve the previous live registry. No-op success refreshes from latest disk and does not rewrite the file. Base import assigns only after all records validate.

Object root and exact numeric schema 1 are required when schemaVersion is present; malformed JSON, wrong typed schema, invalid peer/request container, invalid methods/IDs/params, and duplicate IDs fail closed. Absent version or absent peer remains the existing version-1 compatibility shape. Existing base null-params compatibility is retained, not silently upgraded to stricter business validation.

Approval issue dedup and compatibility runtime-ID response lookup execute inside the fresh-state transaction. Stale registry snapshots are not written as authority; unrelated pending requests and committed answers are loaded before mutation. Healthy unknown responses remain None; storage failure remains Err.

If main is missing, a sole backup survives until the new main rename succeeds. If main exists, prior main is staged to backup and restore is attempted on install failure; failed restore reports the remaining backup. Successful main install is the commit point, so subsequent backup cleanup errors do not falsely report rollback. Temporary file cleanup is scoped to the newly created unique path.

Both writers open the same persistent .lock inode without truncation, reject nonempty legacy sentinels, hold an independent File guard over the complete transaction, retry only the primary fs2 contention OS code for 200 x 10 ms, and unlock without unlinking. Guard construction precedes post-acquire validation so those failures release the acquired lock. No timestamp-based stealing remains.

Static file/backup/lock symlinks and nonregular entries are refused. Opened file metadata is rechecked; Unix verifies device/inode identity. New temp/lock files use private creation modes; chmod is on opened handles. Existing parent directory permissions are not changed. These checks do not establish hostile concurrent path-replacement protection, Windows file identity proof, Windows ACL hardening or parent-symlink containment.

Literal helper-region comparison from read_state_document_unlocked through permissions found identical reader, writer, lock, identity, temp and permission behavior. The only difference is with_state_lock adapting String to ServerRequestError in the peer crate.

The test creates a legal 240-character committed-state component and reaches the actual OS temp-file create error after candidate mutation; it asserts the exact temp-create error phase. Five transitions cover issue, response, clarify partial/final and cancel with live-state/file-byte equality, no temp leakage, repair to a short fixture path, reopen, retry, outcome and subsequent reopen checks. This is one authored test containing five cases, not five independently executed results.

Additional tests inject real fixture directory obstacles through a cfg(test) precommit hook while retaining the real writer, compare prior committed bytes and live export, remove only fixture-owned obstacles, and recover. These hook cases test real path validation failure, not disk-full, fsync error, rename failure or power-cut recovery.

An owned subprocess enters the exact same test using explicit environment and takes the actual OS lock. Parent uses a barrier, exercises timeout while child remains alive with mtime older than 30 seconds, kills only that child, retains the lock inode and retries successfully. It tests owner process death, not system power loss. Its platform behavior still requires Actions.

Authored controls independently exercise base import atomicity, wrapper startup/mutation failure, duplicate IDs, strict schema shape, multiple fresh/stale registries, deletion non-resurrection, approval dedup and lookup, different-question answer merging, and storage-error versus healthy missing-ID separation.
